title: Clarinetist Bichet, Arthur Campbell and the many downtown bands
summary: Bichet played in everyone's band by ear with a gifted tone; Arthur Campbell and Lewis Wade are also praised.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: Oh, he played all of them. At one time he was down there. Played at Piron sometime. Then Mario Perez sometime. I used to play, you see, had so many different bands downtown in that day. All different men had bands. And that day, all you had to do was play and get you a bunch of men together. Played at Jimmy Pileout sometime. He played everybody sometime. But Frank, he played in bands that Frank Kahino was in a lot of times. But he could play everything, anything. He didn't read, but he played everything they played. Anything they played, they played it right now. I don't care what position they play it in. What key they put it in. And that's the most beautiful tone from a cloud, a natural-born cloud from his birth. He was, he was, he didn't need to, he didn't need to know music. He just, that's the extremely gifted musician. In those days, Arthur Campbell was very famous around here then. You heard of him, didn't you, Arthur Campbell?
Yeah, I think he made a couple of records on the band.

Yeah, yeah, yeah. He was good too, Arthur Campbell. He had a strange way, a beautiful way of playing, I thought, Arthur Campbell. Lewis Wade, you heard talk of him? Did you hear talk of Lewis Wade? He's a nice player too.
